## Execution audit

**Provenance.** All citations below refer to expanded files under `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/r2/generic_rsi/C1/`. Their archive is `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/work/scene_archive/bundles/r2--generic_rsi.tar.gz`; each corresponding member is `experiments/scene_rsi_pilot/results/r2/generic_rsi/C1/` followed by the cited relative file path. Line references are to the original expanded files.

### Chaise interior — development/commons_109923183

The step 3 code describes step 2’s head as too narrow and high and attempts to open and lower it. It builds a filleted seat, scaled ball back, swept frame and trim, arms, aprons, four legs, pillow and label, plus paneled walls, curtains and a cane-chair foreground (X0979, `steps/003/build.py`, lines 5–8, 18–155). Linen-matched materials receive wave/ramp color and noise bump; an oak brick/noise material is assigned to meshes whose world bounding-box tops are below .01. This is a selection rule, not a contact test (X0979, lines 160–233). The camera is `(1.05,-4.25,3.15)`, lens 50, with two area lights and AgX (X0979, lines 10–12, 235–244).

Steps 2 and 3 each report successful Blender 4.2.10 renders, 16/16 samples and saved PNG and blend files, with 411 and 384 reported primitives respectively; errors are null and stderr empty (X0978, `steps/002/result.json`, lines 2–7; X0980, `steps/003/result.json`, lines 2–7). The task metadata gives a **reference** size of 512×384, not independently measured output dimensions (X0981, `task.json`, lines 2–5). No selection or quality validation for this scene is supplied.

### Ship compartment — development/commons_118588033

The generated scene represents architecture, a two-color column, three berth levels, ventilated cabinets, lockers, machinery cage, pipes, telephone and pendant assemblies using boxes, rods, balls and swept tubes (X0990, `steps/003/build.py`, lines 24–179). Step 2 raised mattresses and darkened the palette; step 3’s comments identify remaining depth and overlap problems, then move lockers and machinery forward and add cabinet mounting feet (X0988, `steps/002/build.py`, lines 4–9, 51–63; X0990, lines 4–9, 72–84, 94–107, 121–133). Those feet express support intent, not verified physical contact.

The fixed camera is `(0,-3,1.66)` toward `(-.08,4.7,1.64)`, lens 25 and sensor 36. The final code sets procedural deck noise/bump, emission on bright materials, four area lights, ambient strength .16 and AgX (X0990, lines 10–11, 181–218). The three executions report success, saved renders and 238, 241 and 245 primitives, all at 16 samples (X0987, `steps/001/result.json`, lines 2–7; X0989, `steps/002/result.json`, lines 2–7; X0991, `steps/003/result.json`, lines 2–7).

`selected.json` records step 3, although the record’s separate `selected` field is null (X0984, `selected.json`, lines 1–3; X0983, `record.json`, lines 49–57). The record reports valid, overall .4289, SSIM .1892, LPIPS .7556 and functional passes for Architecture; it explicitly limits the functional test to structural/edit operability, with semantic completeness and support collision truth null (X0983, lines 16–34). GPU rendering is recorded; functional evaluation used CPU after the GPU became busy, not a reported rendering failure (X0983, lines 58–68, 156–170).

### Kitchen — selection/commons_133800864

The final build contains window blinds, a paneled cabinet, roll, towel assembly, sink, jug, pitcher and smaller countertop objects (X0993, `build.py`, lines 29–206). Step 2’s comments diagnose step 1’s wall obstructing the camera; the final comments instead identify step 2 cropping and attempt wider framing. These are author observations, not independently inspected images (X0999, `steps/002/build.py`, lines 4–14; X0993, lines 4–13). Final materials use color-matched metallic and plastic settings, procedural granite and fabric/paper noise and bump; camera lens is 58, with two area emitters and AgX (X0993, lines 211–272).

Step 1 actually completed a 16-sample render with 380 reported primitives and no error, despite the later reported obstruction—thus a potentially poor reconstruction, not a technical render failure (X0998, `steps/001/result.json`, lines 2–7). The supplied record reports three executions, completion and null runtime error, but does not include step 2 or 3 result logs (X0994, `record.json`, lines 16, 39–53). Step 3 is recorded in `selected.json`, while `record.json` again has `selected: null` (X0995, lines 1–3; X0994, lines 56–57). Its valid/functional passes and overall .3569 are recorded results, not independent proof of visual quality or physical support; the latter is explicitly untested (X0994, lines 17–34).

No reference or rendered images were supplied for visual inspection. Code coordinates and intended overlaps do not establish contact or image fidelity, and these records contain no independent acceptance judgment.
